```{r}
  id.vars = c("chr", "ps", "af"),
```

## Cumulative position
```{r}
library(dplyr)

long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered <- long_individual_tes_gwas[-log10(long_individual_tes_gwas$p_wald)>3,]

# Simple cumulative position calculation
long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered <- long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered %>%
  arrange(chr, ps) %>%
  group_by(chr) %>%
  mutate(chr_len = max(ps)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(chr_offset = c(0, cumsum(unique(chr_len))[-length(unique(chr_len))])[chr]) %>%
  mutate(ps_cum = ps + chr_offset)

# Convert TE to numeric for tight spacing
long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered <- long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered %>%
  mutate(TE_num = as.numeric(factor(TE)))

# Calculate chromosome centers for x-axis labels
chr_axis <- long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered %>%
  group_by(chr) %>%
  summarize(center = mean(ps_cum))

ggplot(long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered,
       aes(x = ps_cum/1e6, y = TE_num, color = -log10(p_wald))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 4, shape = 15) +
 scale_color_gradient2(low = "#FAF8F1", mid = "#A9B5DF", high = "#2D336B",
                      midpoint = 6,
                      limits = c(3, 10), oob = scales::squish,
                      name = "-log10(P)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = chr_axis$center/1e6, 
                     labels = chr_axis$chr) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Chromosome", y = "TE position") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())

## Join with tes
long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered_with_info <- inner_join(long_individual_tes_gwas_filtered, te_annotation, by=c("TE"="Transposon_Name"))
```

```{r}
# Option 1: Cluster by maximum p-value instead of median
te_order <- long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered %>%
  group_by(TE) %>%
  summarise(max_pval = max(-log10(p_wald), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(max_pval)) %>%
  pull(TE)

# Option 2: Cluster by mean p-value
te_order <- long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered %>%
  group_by(TE) %>%
  summarise(mean_pval = mean(-log10(p_wald), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_pval)) %>%
  pull(TE)

# Option 3: Hierarchical clustering based on p-value patterns across chromosomes
library(cluster)
te_matrix <- long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered %>%
  select(TE, chr, p_wald) %>%
  group_by(TE, chr) %>%
  summarise(mean_pval = mean(-log10(p_wald), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = chr, values_from = mean_pval, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("TE")

hc <- hclust(dist(te_matrix))
te_order <- rownames(te_matrix)[hc$order]



# Apply the hierarchical clustering order to your data
long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered$TE <- 
  factor(long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered$TE, 
         levels = te_order)

# Your original plot with clustered TE order
ggplot(long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered,
       aes(x = ps/1e6, y = TE, color = -log10(p_wald))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 0.6) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#FAF0E6",
    mid = "#B9B4C7", 
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 5,
    limits = c(4, 12),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "-log10(P)"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete() +
  labs(x = "Position (Mbp)", y = "TE (Hierarchically Clustered)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 3),
    panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

## Join wtiht TE
te_annotation <- fread("/groups/nordborg/projects/ddm1_resilencing/11_resources/ref_genome/TAIR10_Transposable_Elements.txt")
long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered_with_te_info <- inner_join(long_individual_tes_gwas_with_heritability_filtered,te_annotation,by=c("TE"="Transposon_Name"))
```

# Option 1: Filter NAs within summarise
library(dplyr)
library(metap)

fisher_results <- long_individual_tes_gwas %>%
  group_by(chr, ps) %>%
  summarise(
    fisher_combined_p = {
      valid_p <- p_wald[!is.na(p_wald) & p_wald > 0 & p_wald <= 1]
      if (length(valid_p) > 0) {
        sumlog(valid_p)$p
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    n_TEs = sum(!is.na(p_wald)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Heatmap of individual TE gwas
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(viridis)
library(data.table)

# Assuming your data is already loaded as 'long_individual_tes_gwas'
# If you need to load it, uncomment and modify the path below:
# long_individual_tes_gwas <- fread("your_file_path.csv")

# Data preparation for heatmap
prepare_gwas_heatmap <- function(gwas_data, significance_threshold = 0.05) {
  
  # Filter for significant results (optional)
  # gwas_filtered <- gwas_data[p_wald < significance_threshold]
  
  # Create genomic position (combine chr and ps)
  gwas_data[, genomic_pos := paste0("chr", chr, "_", ps)]
  
  # Convert p-values to -log10 for better visualization
  gwas_data[, neg_log10_p := -log10(p_wald)]
  
  # Create bins for genomic positions if too many SNPs
  # This helps with visualization when you have many positions
  gwas_data[, pos_bin := cut(ps, breaks = 20, labels = FALSE), by = chr]
  gwas_data[, binned_pos := paste0("chr", chr, "_bin", pos_bin)]
  
  return(gwas_data)
}

# Prepare the data
gwas_prepared <- prepare_gwas_heatmap(long_individual_tes_gwas)

# Create heatmap - Option 1: Using genomic positions vs TEs
create_gwas_heatmap_v1 <- function(gwas_data, top_n_tes = 50) {
  
  # Select top TEs by minimum p-value
  top_tes <- gwas_data[, .(min_p = min(p_wald)), by = TE][order(min_p)][1:top_n_tes]$TE
  
  # Filter data for top TEs
  plot_data <- gwas_data[TE %in% top_tes]
  
  # Create the heatmap
  p1 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = binned_pos, y = TE, fill = neg_log10_p)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "-log10(p)", option = "plasma") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "GWAS Trans-effects Heatmap",
      subtitle = paste("Top", top_n_tes, "TEs by significance"),
      x = "Genomic Position (Binned)",
      y = "Transposable Elements"
    )
  
  return(p1)
}

# Create heatmap - Option 2: Chromosome-based view
create_gwas_heatmap_v2 <- function(gwas_data, top_n_tes = 30) {
  
  # Select top TEs
  top_tes <- gwas_data[, .(min_p = min(p_wald)), by = TE][order(min_p)][1:top_n_tes]$TE
  
  # Aggregate by chromosome and TE
  chr_te_summary <- gwas_data[TE %in% top_tes, 
                              .(mean_neg_log10_p = mean(neg_log10_p),
                                min_p = min(p_wald),
                                n_snps = .N), 
                              by = .(chr, TE)]
  
  p2 <- ggplot(chr_te_summary, aes(x = factor(chr), y = TE, fill = mean_neg_log10_p)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Mean\n-log10(p)", option = "plasma") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "GWAS Trans-effects by Chromosome",
      subtitle = paste("Top", top_n_tes, "TEs - Mean significance per chromosome"),
      x = "Chromosome",
      y = "Transposable Elements"
    )
  
  return(p2)
}

# Generate the heatmaps
heatmap_v1 <- create_gwas_heatmap_v1(gwas_prepared, top_n_tes = 50)
heatmap_v2 <- create_gwas_heatmap_v2(gwas_prepared, top_n_tes = 30)

# Display the heatmaps
print(heatmap_v1)
print(heatmap_v2)

# Save the plots
ggsave("gwas_trans_effects_heatmap_v1.png", heatmap_v1, 
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
ggsave("gwas_trans_effects_heatmap_v2.png", heatmap_v2, 
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# Additional analysis: Summary statistics
cat("\n=== GWAS Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Total SNPs:", nrow(gwas_prepared), "\n")
cat("Unique TEs:", length(unique(gwas_prepared$TE)), "\n")
cat("Chromosomes:", paste(unique(gwas_prepared$chr), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Significant associations (p < 0.05):", sum(gwas_prepared$p_wald < 0.05), "\n")
cat("Highly significant associations (p < 0.001):", sum(gwas_prepared$p_wald < 0.001), "\n")

# Top 10 most significant associations
top_associations <- gwas_prepared[order(p_wald)][1:10, .(chr, ps, TE, p_wald, neg_log10_p)]
cat("\n=== Top 10 Most Significant Associations ===\n")
print(top_associations)

```

## Cluster TEs together 
```{r}
# Step 1: Create a matrix for clustering based on signal patterns
te_signal_matrix <- sig_peaks_ann2 %>%
  # Create bins or use existing genomic positions
  mutate(pos_bin = round(ps / 1e6, 1)) %>%  # 100kb bins
  select(TE, chr, pos_bin, pwald_log10) %>%
  # Create a wide matrix: TE x genomic_position
  unite("chr_pos", chr, pos_bin, sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = chr_pos,
    values_from = pwald_log10,
    values_fill = 0,  # Fill missing with 0
    values_fn = max  # If multiple values, take max
  )

# Step 2: Prepare matrix for clustering
te_matrix <- te_signal_matrix %>%
  column_to_rownames("TE") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Step 3: Hierarchical clustering
te_dist <- dist(te_matrix, method = "euclidean")
te_hclust <- hclust(te_dist, method = "complete")

# Step 4: Get clustered order
te_clustered_order <- rownames(te_matrix)[te_hclust$order]

# Step 5: Apply clustering order to your data
sig_peaks_ann_clustered <- sig_peaks_ann2 %>%
  mutate(TE = factor(TE, levels = te_clustered_order))

# Step 6: Plot with clustered order
ggplot(sig_peaks_ann_clustered, aes(x = ps / 1e6, y = TE)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = pwald_log10), alpha = 0.4, size = 0.3) +
  geom_point(
    data = subset(sig_peaks_ann_clustered, highlight_gene),
    aes(x = ps / 1e6, y = TE, color = pwald_log10),
    shape = 17, size = 3, stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~chr, scales = "free_x", ncol = 5) +
  labs(
    x = "Genomic Position (Mbp)",
    y = "Transposon (Clustered)",
    color = "-log10(p-value)",
    title = "TE GWAS Results - Hierarchically Clustered"
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#FAF0E6", mid = "#B9B4C7", high = "red",
    midpoint = 5, limits = c(4, 10), oob = scales::squish
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 3),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}

# Check your p-values first
clean_p_values <- long_individual_tes_gwas$p_wald[!is.na(long_individual_tes_gwas$p_wald)]
result_clean <- fishers_method_robust(clean_p_values)
print(result_clean)

# Improved Fisher's method with better numerical handling
fishers_method_robust <- function(p_values) {
  # Remove NA values and problematic p-values
  valid_p <- p_values[!is.na(p_values) & p_values > 0 & p_values < 1]
  
  if(length(valid_p) == 0) {
    return(list(combined_p = NA, test_stat = NA, n_tests = 0))
  }
  
  # Fisher's method: -2 * sum(log(p))
  test_stat <- -2 * sum(log(valid_p))
  df <- 2 * length(valid_p)
  
  # Use pchisq with lower.tail=FALSE for better numerical precision
  combined_p <- pchisq(test_stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  return(list(
    combined_p = combined_p,
    test_stat = test_stat,
    n_tests = length(valid_p),
    log10_combined_p = -log10(combined_p)
  ))
}

# Test with robust version
result_robust <- fishers_method_robust(long_individual_tes_gwas$p_wald)
print(result_robust)

# If still 0, check the test statistic magnitude
print(paste("Test statistic:", result_robust$test_stat))
print(paste("Is test stat very large?", result_robust$test_stat > 100))
```

```{r}
  group_by(Transposon_Name, chr, cluster_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cluster_hits = n(),
    cluster_start = min(ps),
    cluster_end = max(ps),
    max_signal = max(max_signal),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_cluster_hits > 1)
```

### Visualize trans peaks
```{r}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(pheatmap)

sig_peaks_ann_ltr <-sig_peaks_ann[sig_peaks_ann$Transposon_Super_Family=='LTR/Gypsy',]
dt <- sig_peaks_ann

# Bin positions within each chromosome
dt <- dt %>%
  group_by(chr) %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(ps, breaks=20, labels=FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create a combined bin label
dt <- dt %>%
  mutate(chr_bin = paste0("chr", chr, "_bin", bin))

# Create a matrix: rows = TEs, columns = bins, values = mean(pwald_log10)
heatmap_data <- dt %>%
  group_by(Transposon_Name, chr_bin) %>%
  summarize(value = mean(pwald_log10, na.rm=TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = chr_bin, values_from = value, values_fill = 0)

# Set rownames
heatmap_data <- as.data.frame(heatmap_data)
rownames(heatmap_data) <- heatmap_data$Transposon_Name
heatmap_data$Transposon_Name <- NULL

# Order columns by chromosome and bin
col_order <- gsub("chr", "", colnames(heatmap_data))
chr_num <- as.numeric(sub("_bin.*", "", col_order))
bin_num <- as.numeric(sub(".*_bin", "", col_order))
order_idx <- order(chr_num, bin_num)
mat <- as.matrix(heatmap_data[, order_idx])

# Plot heatmap without clustering
# Define breaks
breaks <- c(0, 5, 10, max(mat, na.rm=TRUE))

# Define colors for each interval
colors <- c("white", "blue", "red", "darkred")
library(scales)
custom_palette <- c(
  rep("white", 20),      # 0 to 6
  rep("#EEF296", 20),    # 6 to 8
  rep("#9ADE7B", 30),    # 8 to 10
  rep("#508D69", 30)     # 10 to max
)


pheatmap(mat,
         cluster_rows = FALSE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         show_rownames = TRUE,   # Set to TRUE if you want to see TE names
         show_colnames = FALSE,  # Set to TRUE if you want to see bin labels
         color = custom_palette)
```

```{r}
# Install and load required packages
# install.packages("metap")
# install.packages("data.table")
# install.packages("ggplot2")
library(metap)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

# Get all p-value columns
# Define your threshold (e.g., 1e-20)


# Filter rows using apply()
p_value_columns <- grep("^p_wald", names(individual_tes_gwas), value = TRUE)


##Identify SNPs with extreme pvalues

# Function to combine p-values using Fisher's method from metap
log_fisher_combine <- function(p_values) {
  p_values <- pmax(p_values, 1e-300)  # Avoid log(0)
  log_p <- log(p_values)
  chi_stat <- -2 * sum(log_p)
  
  if (chi_stat > 30000) {  # Threshold to prevent underflow
    return(-Inf)  # Represents p = 0 in log-space
  } else {
    df <- 2 * length(p_values)
    pchisq(chi_stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
  }
}


# Apply the function to combine p-values
individual_tes_gwas$combined_p <- apply(individual_tes_gwas[, ..p_value_columns], 1, log_fisher_combine)

# Prepare data for Manhattan plot

manhattan_data <- individual_tes_gwas[, .(chr, ps, combined_p)] # Sort
manhattan_data <- manhattan_data[!is.na(combined_p)] # Remove NA 
manhattan_data$chr <- as.factor(manhattan_data$chr)

# Order chromosomes and calculate cumulative position
setorder(manhattan_data, chr, ps)
chr_lengths <- manhattan_data[, .(chr_len = max(ps)), by = chr]
chr_lengths$cum_len <- cumsum(as.numeric(chr_lengths$chr_len)) - chr_lengths$chr_len
manhattan_data <- merge(manhattan_data, chr_lengths, by = "chr")
manhattan_data$pos_cum <- manhattan_data$ps + manhattan_data$cum_len

# Axis labels for chromosomes
axis_df <- manhattan_data[, .(center = mean(pos_cum)), by = chr]

# Manhattan plot
manhattan_data$neg_log10_p <- -manhattan_data$combined_p / log(10)


ggplot(manhattan_data, aes(x = pos_cum, y = (neg_log10_p), color = as.factor(as.numeric(chr) %% 2))) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#393E46", "#A78295")) +
  scale_x_continuous(label = axis_df$chr, breaks = axis_df$center) +
  labs(x = "Chromosome", y = "-log10(p)", title = "Manhattan Plot") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15 ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()) 
  #geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(5e-8), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") # Optional: genome-wide significance line



## Make a qqplot
p_sorted <- sort(manhattan_data$combined_p)

# 2. Calculate expected p-values
# Assuming manhattan_data has combined_p column (Fisher's combined p-values)

# 1. First sort the p-values
sorted_p <- sort(manhattan_data$combined_p)

# 2. Calculate expected and observed correctly
n <- length(sorted_p)
expected <- -log10(seq(0.5/n, 1-0.5/n, length.out=n))  # expected uniform
observed <- -log10(sorted_p)  # observed values

# 3. Create dataframe for plotting
qq_data <- data.frame(
    expected = expected,
    observed = observed
)

# 4. Plot with ggplot2
ggplot(qq_data, aes(x=expected, y=observed)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, color="red", linetype="dashed") +
    labs(
        x = "Expected -log10(p)",
        y = "Observed -log10(p)",
        title = "QQ Plot of Fisher's Combined P-values"
    ) +
    theme_bw()
```

```{r}
# Retrieve gene annotation data
annotation_tair10 <- getBM(
  attributes = c(
    "chromosome_name",
    "start_position",
    "end_position",
    "gene_biotype",
    "ensembl_gene_id",
    "external_gene_name",
```

## Map to the genes 
```{r}

manhattan_data$neg_log10_p <- as.numeric(manhattan_data$neg_log10_p)
significant_snps <-manhattan_data[manhattan_data$neg_log10_p>100,]
```

```{r}
max_upstream_distance <- 100  # Adjust as necessary
max_downstream_distance <- 100  # Adjust as necessary
snps_near_genes <- vector("list", length = nrow(significant_snps))
# Loop through each SNP to find if it's inside, upstream, or downstream of any gene
for (i in 1:nrow(significant_snps)) {
  snp <- significant_snps[i, ]
  genes_on_chr <- annotation_tair10[annotation_tair10$chromosome_name == snp$chr, ]
  is_near_or_inside_gene <- (genes_on_chr$start_position - max_upstream_distance <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$end_position + max_downstream_distance) |
    (genes_on_chr$start_position <= snp$ps & snp$ps <= genes_on_chr$end_position)
  
  if (any(is_near_or_inside_gene)) {
    temp_df <- genes_on_chr[is_near_or_inside_gene, ]
    temp_df$snp_position <- snp$ps
    temp_df$chromosome <- snp$chr 
    #temp_df$af <- snp$af
    #temp_df$variance_explained <- snp$r_squared
    temp_df$pval <- -log10(snp$neg_log10_p)
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- temp_df
  } else {
    snps_near_genes[[i]] <- NULL
  }
}

snps_near_genes_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(snps_near_genes, function(df) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  df
}))
```
